LinkedIn support for companies and founders

A social media virtual assistant can keep LinkedIn content and conversations organised. We use approved company page access and prepare personal profile content for the account owner to review.

Page and profile upkeep

A marketing virtual assistant can review the company description, headline, featured links and banner against approved positioning. Prepare profile updates and use company page roles for changes in scope.

Publishing and thought leadership

Build a calendar around audience questions, events and launches. Draft founder posts, company updates, newsletters, articles and document carousels. Prepare images, mentions and links before scheduling approved posts.

Engagement and inbox handoff

Your social media virtual assistant monitors agreed comments, mentions and page messages. Prepare replies using the brand’s guidance, flag sensitive questions and pass enquiries to the CRM owner.

Research and performance

Review relevant topics, hashtags, competitor activity and audience questions. Report impressions, engagement, clicks and follower changes with dates and post links, then suggest topics for the next review.

Social media marketing and community support

A social media virtual assistant can turn a campaign into a calendar with channel-specific formats, approvals and reporting. Agree who owns the strategy, publishing access and response rules.

Plan content by channel

A digital marketing virtual assistant can research audience questions, trends and hashtags, curate useful references and map posts for LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook and other agreed channels around campaign dates.

Create and repurpose assets

Draft captions, posts and approved copy. Create Canva graphics, flyers and carousels and edit short videos or clips with captions. Adapt each item to the channel, rights and accessibility requirements.

Schedule, engage and moderate

A social media virtual assistant checks the approved version, links and timing before scheduling posts. Monitor messages and comments, moderate under brand rules and route sensitive conversations for review.

Coordinate creators and campaigns

A marketing virtual assistant can research creators and partners, prepare outreach and track deliverables and paid campaign assets. The campaign owner approves spend, targeting, contracts and commitments.

Measure and improve

A digital marketing virtual assistant can report reach, engagement, clicks and publishing consistency by channel and campaign. Your team can compare formats and decide which themes merit another test.

Content writing, creative production and email marketing

Bring the source material, approved claims and reviewer. An email marketing virtual assistant can coordinate a newsletter from draft and test send through approval and scheduling.

Writing, editing and ghostwriting

A marketing virtual assistant can research, draft and edit articles, blogs, guides, website copy and newsletters. Ghostwrite against approved examples, verify sources and retain the review record. See how agencies and publishers organise editorial work.

Design, video and podcast coordination

Organise creative assets, prepare branded graphics and flyers, edit approved clips, coordinate guest or crew schedules and prepare show notes, transcripts and publishing files.

Email campaigns and newsletter operations

An email marketing virtual assistant prepares templates, clean subscriber lists, approved segments, nurture sequences and test sends. Check audience, subject, links, forms and timing, record approval and report results.

Where this helps day to day.

Your social media virtual assistant needs channel rules and final assets. An email marketing virtual assistant also needs approved recipients, links and review dates.

Drafts are stuck in review.

Give each piece one reviewer, a due date and a place to record the decision.

Assets live in too many folders.

Create a source list and distinguish the approved versions from working files.

A newsletter is ready to send.

Verify the audience, links and preview. Record the approval before scheduling.

What the finished handoff looks like.

A marketing virtual assistant should show what is ready and what is waiting. Your digital marketing virtual assistant can link the current preview and approval. This example uses fictional records.

What to verify before closing a task.

A digital marketing virtual assistant should verify links, versions and dates. An email marketing virtual assistant should check the approved subject, audience and destination.

  • Confirm the reviewer has approved the current version.
  • Verify links, images and rights before publication.
  • Check channel-specific formatting and mobile previews.
  • Record the final live URL and flag missing assets.

Take a campaign item from brief to release

Your social media virtual assistant can coordinate posts around a campaign page. Your marketing virtual assistant should mark the dependency when a release date changes.

A marketing team plans an email and a social post from one approved article. Both use an image that is still under review. The workflow needs to preserve the source copy, make the different versions easy to review and prevent either item from going live before the asset is cleared.

  1. 01

    Turn the request into an editorial item

    Record the audience, objective, source article, two output formats and final reviewer. Split the deliverables into separate tasks with one shared dependency for the image. A calendar date alone does not say what is ready to ship.

  2. 02

    Prepare previews in the correct channels

    Adapt the approved material to the agreed length and format. Attach previews and the current asset version to the review item. Flag any change to a claim or promise so the reviewer can distinguish it from routine formatting.

  3. 03

    Release the approved version

    Check the approval against the specific draft, link destinations and publication time zone. After scheduling or publishing, record the final link and update the calendar. Carry any unapproved derivative forward as a separate item.

Prepare the inputs and rules.

A marketing virtual assistant needs a current brand example. Your email marketing virtual assistant should also see a reviewed newsletter before preparing the first draft.

Marketing virtual assistant brief template

Use fields for audience, format, objective, due date and approver. Show a completed example so the marketing virtual assistant can tell when source material or a decision is missing.

Digital marketing virtual assistant asset library

Identify the folder or system that holds approved copy, images and templates. Use version names that a reviewer can recognise without comparing several files by eye.

Social media virtual assistant publication rules

Confirm who can schedule or publish, which channels require preview links, and how to record approval. Agree when a time-sensitive exception should go to the campaign owner.

Decide what happens when the normal rule fails.

Your digital marketing virtual assistant should flag conflicting feedback. A social media virtual assistant needs confirmation before replacing an approved scheduled asset.

An asset lacks permission to publish

Keep the item in review and note what evidence is missing. Offer an approved alternative only if the reviewer can confirm that it fits the brief.

Two reviewers send conflicting edits

Record both requests against the current draft and route them to the final approver. Do not schedule a version while the decision is open.

A date moves after scheduling

Check dependent items and time zones, update the calendar and ask the channel owner to confirm the new date before replacing the scheduled version.

Check the work against the original brief.

Review the output from your marketing virtual assistant against the brief. Your email marketing virtual assistant can record the changes needed for the next send.

Approval trace

Pick a published item and follow it back to the approved draft, asset and reviewer. If any link is missing, improve how the handoff is recorded.

Release readiness

Look at the next week’s calendar and distinguish ready items from drafts waiting on an asset, review or decision. Assign someone to each blocked item.

Reuse quality

Compare a derivative with its source. Confirm that headlines, links and claims remain accurate for the intended channel and audience.

Leave a record the next person can use.

A social media virtual assistant should leave the final asset and schedule together. Your digital marketing virtual assistant should also link any open approval.

Part of the handoverWhat to recordWhat the next owner can do
Current workWhat to recordInclude the latest version, the source link and the current status. Note what was already checked and which changes were approved.What the next owner can doContinue from the latest approved state without searching for the source or repeating a completed check.
Open decisionsWhat to recordList each outstanding decision, the person who can make it and the point at which the next owner should follow up.What the next owner can doPrioritise the blocked items and ask a specific question when the next approval is due.
Time-sensitive commitmentsWhat to recordState the time zone, the next update due and any commitments that someone has already shared. Include the agreed backup contact.What the next owner can doKeep the next promise visible and make sure requests that cannot wait reach the correct person.
Changes to the instructionsWhat to recordRecord which rule changed, who approved it and when it starts. Keep an example that shows the difference in practice.What the next owner can doUse the current rule and compare new work with the agreed example during the next review.

Plan social media virtual assistant publishing

Agree cutoffs with your marketing virtual assistant. Your email marketing virtual assistant needs enough time for previews, links and audience review.

Recurring publishing

Give each channel a cutoff for approved copy and assets. Reserve a separate window for formatting, checking links and building previews. A schedule with both dates makes it easier to see whether the review queue or the production queue is causing a delay.

Launch weeks

Mark items that rely on a single go-live decision. Keep the final creative, web destination and campaign tracking together, and decide whether related posts should move as a group if a page slips.

Late changes

Record who can approve a different date or a last-minute copy change. Keep the old version linked for reference and verify that the new change is reflected wherever the item was scheduled.

Frequently Asked Questions

Ask which tools your digital marketing virtual assistant will use. A social media virtual assistant also needs clear publishing permissions and an escalation contact.

Can you work with our existing brand guidelines?

Use a brand handoff with example copy, asset locations, approval owners and any claims that need review.

Who signs off before publication?

Name one reviewer and define how their approval is recorded before an item is scheduled.

Can you turn one approved piece into several formats?

Agree which versions are in scope, such as a newsletter excerpt or social post. Route changes in claims or tone back to the reviewer.

How are assets and versions tracked?

Use the agreed folder or project board to record the current draft, the approved assets and the final published link.

What happens when a brief is missing an asset or decision?

Flag the missing item, assign an owner and show which publication date it affects. Resume when the required material is approved.

Can you run paid ads or define our strategy?

Scope execution separately from strategy, ad spend and specialist production. Identify who owns budget and performance decisions.
